subject: ventures/3d-print-price-calculator
professional: a person who runs a paid 3D print farm or small service bureau and sells parts on Etsy/Shopify; they check first that the per-part cost carries filament (with waste), machine-hour cost (power plus depreciation plus maintenance), failed attempts and labour, that the marketplace fee used is the real fee schedule (percentage and fixed per-order parts), that the listed price actually lands on the target margin after that fee, and that grams and hours pulled from the slicer match what the slicer reports

evidence.verification: cd ventures/3d-print-price-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 77 tests, 77 pass (237 ms, Node 22.23.4). Eight mutations seeded with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 5 caught (failure multiplier 1/(1-f) -> 1+f, electricity /1000 -> /100, failure buffer dropped from total, break-even fee multiplied instead of divided, Cura density hard-coded), 3 survived: otherFixedCost dropped from the total (calc.mjs:121, a user input silently ignored), Cura ;TIME overriding a PrusaSlicer time (gcode.mjs:60), and Simplify3D weight overriding PrusaSlicer grams (gcode.mjs:68). No test asserts totalCost or the suggested price as a number, only identities between outputs, so a wrong component that the identities don't cover passes.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (163 lines, pure, documented), gcode.mjs (90 lines, pure, no I/O, tested), index.html module script (lines 105-254), usage.mjs, share.mjs headers, calc.test.mjs, gcode.test.mjs. Clean separation of arithmetic from DOM, textContent output (no innerHTML of user data), head/tail 256 KB file read for large G-code. Defects: number() accepts '' as 0 (calc.mjs:25-30), so blank required fields are silent zeros; fees and depreciation use floats with display rounding only (fine at these magnitudes).
evidence.claims: Disclaimer and no-warranty present on all four pages; independence from slicer vendors stated; the arithmetic claims (fee-solved price, failure buffer only on per-attempt costs, Cura grams derived and disclosed) are backed by calc.mjs/gcode.mjs and tests. Not backed: README.md:55-56 'nothing is saved when you close the tab -- every field resets on refresh by design' is false: the page has a Save button that writes to localStorage and restores the draft on load (index.html:202-240). vs-slicer-cost-estimate.html:86 'It does not read your slicer ... you bring the grams and the hours' contradicts the G-code import the main page ships (also on the served page). index.html:87 and README.md:57 list three counted events, but the page records six (also scenario_saved, link_copied, sponsor_link_clicked); all stay local, so this is a disclosure gap, not a leak. The H1 and title target Etsy, but the default 'Marketplace + payment fee' 8.5% (index.html:44, calc.mjs:45) is uncited and below Etsy's US schedule. Source llms.txt points at github.io but the served llms.txt points at marisstella.app (build rewrite, source-only, not filed).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job of an Etsy maker pricing a 45 g, 3 h PLA part: import the PrusaSlicer G-code, keep the defaults, read $9.72 suggested and $6.00 break-even, then check a competitor's $8 price in the check panel. This works in a minute and the breakdown is clear. First-hour hits for a seller: Etsy's per-order fixed fees ($0.25 processing + $0.20 listing) have to be folded into 'Other flat cost' by hand and the page doesn't say so; one print = one part, so a plate of 12 keychains needs the user to divide grams and hours themselves; there is no shipping-on-fee handling (Etsy charges 6.5% on shipping too). Usable for its stated audience with those limits.
evidence.domain: Compared against print-farm costing practice (a machine-hour rate covering depreciation, power and maintenance/consumables, plus material with purge waste, plus labour for plate changes and finishing, plus a scrap allowance, plus the marketplace's actual fee schedule) and Etsy's US Fees and Payments Policy as I know it (6.5% transaction fee on item plus shipping, 3% + $0.25 payment processing, $0.20 listing; etsy.com/legal/fees returned 403 through the proxy, so this is from the published schedule as remembered, not fetched). The structure is right and the fee-solved price is the correct algebra. Departures: at the default suggested $9.72, Etsy's real fees are $1.37 not $0.83, so profit is $2.86 and margin 29.4% instead of the promised 35%; a correct Etsy solve gives $10.71. The failure model charges every failed attempt the full print's material and hours, whereas most failures are caught partway (overcharges, conservative). No maintenance/consumables (nozzles, PEI sheets, belts) in the machine rate, and no batch/plate allocation. Default printer $250 over 3000 h and 120 W are plausible for a hobby bed-slinger.

defects.what: The page is pitched at Etsy sellers but the default 'Marketplace + payment fee' is an uncited 8.5% with no fixed per-order part. Under Etsy's US schedule (6.5% + 3% + $0.25 + $0.20 listing) the default suggested $9.72 earns 29.4%, not the 35% the page says it 'lands on'; the correct solve is $10.71. The page note mentions a listing fee but not the $0.25 processing fee or the 6.5% on shipping.
README says 'nothing is saved when you close the tab -- every field resets on refresh by design', but the page ships Save/Forget buttons that persist and restore the scenario from localStorage.
Comparison page says 'It does not read your slicer ... you bring the grams and the hours', contradicting the G-code import on the main page (served as-is).
Page and README say only three events are counted; index.html also records scenario_saved, link_copied and sponsor_link_clicked (all local-only).

Three of eight seeded mutations survive: dropping otherFixedCost from the total (a user input silently ignored), and two G-code precedence changes. No test pins totalCost or suggestedPrice to a number, only identities between outputs.
number() treats an empty string as 0 (Number('') === 0), so clearing grams, printer cost or the fee on the page yields a lower price with no error.

Bambu Studio/OrcaSlicer header puts 'total estimated time:' after '; model printing time: ...;' on one line; the anchored regex misses it, so a file without the PrusaSlicer-style footer yields no print time.

Failure model charges each failed attempt the full print's filament and hours, though most failures are caught partway, and the machine rate has no maintenance/consumables; both are undisclosed modelling choices.

verdict: The arithmetic is right: every output I recomputed by hand for the default print and for the failed-print page's 5%/25% table matches to the cent, the fee-solved price is the correct algebra, Cura length-to-grams matches PLA's published 1.24 g/cm3 (336 m/kg), and a realistic two-extruder PrusaSlicer footer reads correctly. It does not meet the bar because claims and verification are 2: the README says nothing is saved though the page has a localStorage Save button, the comparison page says the tool does not read your slicer though it imports G-code, the counted-event list is incomplete, and three of eight seeded mutations survive (otherFixedCost can be dropped from the total with all 77 tests green). The domain gap a print-shop seller would hit first is the uncited 8.5% default fee with no fixed part: on Etsy's US schedule the suggested price earns 29.4%, not the 35% it promises. Correctness, completeness, craft and fitness 3; verification, claims and domain 2.
